about: HOW THE TRAINER TRAINS: its settings, as data. The trainers read this and nothing of it is written into their code. A configuration can carry its own values over these (`policy` in its record under training/states/), set by a person.

questions.about: How many questions of each kind a pass asks: its train questions, taken one at a time, and its held questions, which measure it. EACH, or --each, names another number for one run.

loop.about: Training goes question by question (training/loop.mjs), and a question stays in hand until its answer is good (right by the question's own standard, or equivalent to an answer the larger model agrees with itself on): changes are tried best first, from the closest arrangement open, and one that comes closer is built on at once. It never moves on before; where every arrangement open has been tried the search widens, and the arrangements found so far are tried first. cap: a bound on the changes tried on one question (none). classKeep: a change is kept when the questions of its class got better with it (docs/swoa-parity.md): every train question of the class is scored with the change and as the swarm stands, and it is kept when the mean gain is more than twice its paired error and at least classMinGain, no kind of question falls by more than classMargin, and the held questions of the class do not fall by more than their error. classRace: how many questions of the class, drawn evenly from its kinds, a change is scored on first; the rest are asked only where those did not fall. classTries: how many changes a class are proposed for the class outright at the end of a pass, those that most often brought its questions closer. guard: without classKeep, how many questions already good are asked again before a change is kept (it is kept only if none is lost). drop: a change tried on this many questions that made none good is no longer tried (none). beam: where the loop's own policy starts (training/loop-policy.mjs), which the larger model then tunes as training runs: how many closer arrangements are kept open.

plan.about: What the plan lists first: how many arrangements one change from here, how many that are several changes from here at once (wild), and how many changes each of those is (depth).

moves.about: How much each kind of move counts for when the plan ranks what to try.

ratchet.about: A bar that is held tightens: a kind of question the swarm has been at parity on, on the held questions, for this many passes in a row is asked more of (half as many again, each time, up to max times).
